01.r: A warning to watch one's own thoughts.
01.n: Gesenius gives the verb's first sense as TO KEEP, TO WATCH, TO GUARD; this form is reflexive, 'guard yourself, be on your guard'.

02.r: Turns the warning on the hearer himself.
02.n: Literally 'for you', with 'you' singular. Only YLT renders it.

03.r: Names the danger to be avoided.
03.n: Gesenius explains the word as properly a noun of removing, which became a word of prohibiting or hindering, like Greek μή, 'lest'.

04.r: The thought might come to exist in the heart.

05.r: A thought put into words in the heart.
05.n: Literally 'a word'; the next words show it is something said inwardly, so most translations make it 'a thought'. YLT keeps 'a word'.

06.n: Literally 'with your heart': the thought is present with the heart, in its company.

07.r: The inner self, where thoughts and intentions form.
07.n: BDB gives inner man, mind, will, heart, and notes that this form of the word points especially to the mind.

08.r: Describes the thought as base and useless.
08.n: Literally a noun, 'worthlessness': 'a word of worthlessness'. Gesenius explains it as made of 'not' and 'profit', so properly unprofitableness, worthlessness, what is useless.

09.n: Literally 'to say', the usual Hebrew way of introducing quoted words.

10.r: The year of remission is close, so a loan now would soon be lost.
10.n: Gesenius gives TO APPROACH, TO COME NEAR, especially of time, and cites this verse. The perfect, 'has drawn near', presents the year as already almost here. The reasoning about the loan is the plain sense of the warning, though the verse does not spell it out.

11.r: The seventh year of the cycle.

12.n: Literally 'the year of the seven': the number stands for 'seventh'. The brief's lexicon notes that it can serve as an ordinal.

13.r: The same year, named again by what happens in it.

14.r: The letting go of debts in the seventh year.
14.n: Gesenius cites this verse for 'the year of remission', in which debts were to be remitted.

15.r: Looking on the poor man with ill will.
15.n: BDB: be evil, bad. 'Your eye be evil against' him is a Hebrew way of describing a grudging, unkind look; the BSB's 'begrudgingly' takes it so, which is a reasonable reading. The Gesenius entry matched to this verb belongs to a different word spelled alike and does not apply here.
t: so that you look upon ... begrudgingly

16.r: Your way of looking at him.
16.n: Counted with 'be evil': 'and your eye be evil' renders the verb and its subject together.

17.n: The brief's lexicon lists brother, relative, and one of the same tribe; here it most likely means a fellow Israelite, which is a reading of the context.

18.r: Describes the brother: he is in want.
18.n: The same word as 'needy one' in Deuteronomy 15:4. Gesenius gives needy, poor, so called from the idea of needing. It stands after 'your brother' with the article: 'your brother, the needy one'.

20.r: The loan the poor man needs and is refused.
20.n: The ordinary verb for giving; the DRC makes it 'to lend', which is what the passage is about.

22.r: The poor man appeals to God over the refusal.
22.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as TO CRY OUT, TO CALL. A perfect with 'and', continuing what the hearer is warned against; YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'he hath called'.

23.r: His cry accuses the one who refused him.

24.r: Marks the LORD as the one appealed to.

25.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

26.r: The result: guilt rests on the one who refused.
t: and you will be guilty of

27.r: The guilt is counted against you.
27.n: Gesenius cites this verse for the phrase 'to be sin in someone': for him to be reckoned guilty in the matter.

28.r: A wrong for which you are held guilty.
28.n: Gesenius gives sin, fault; BDB adds guilt of sin.

_extra.5: κρυπτὸν (hidden): added by the Greek translators, 'a hidden word'.
_extra.45: μεγάλη (great): added by the Greek translators, 'a great sin'.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the brief gives none.

05.n: ῥῆμα, 'word, saying', a close match for the Hebrew 'word'.

08.n: ἀνόμημα, 'a lawless act': the Greek makes the worthless word a breach of the law.

10.n: Printed Ἐηίζει in our Greek text, a misreading of Ἐγγίζει, 'draws near'. Dictionary form supplied by hand.

15.n: πονηρεύομαι, 'to act wickedly': 'and your eye act wickedly'.

20.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the brief gives none.

22.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the brief gives none. καταβοάω, 'to cry out against'; it has no Strong's number, as it does not occur in the New Testament.

28.n: ἁμαρτία, 'sin', the usual New Testament word.
